title: Los Gatos
name: Los Gatos
metaTitle: Los Gatos 1031 Exchange Investors | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange guidance for Los Gatos investors weighing boutique retail on North Santa Cruz Avenue, Netflix-adjacent office, and creek-trail multifamily.

sections.html: Los Gatos trades on a small-town, foothill identity that has almost nothing to do with the office parks and R&D campuses a few miles down the valley floor, and an exchanger who prices Los Gatos property against San Jose or Santa Clara comps is comparing two different markets. An exchanger coming from a larger office-park submarket should expect smaller deal sizes and a thinner set of comparable sales here than almost anywhere else in the metro.

sections.heading: Netflix's Headquarters Doesn't Change the Town's Retail Character
sections.html:
Netflix has kept its corporate headquarters in Los Gatos for years, a notable exception to the town's otherwise low-rise, boutique commercial character. That single large employer supports some local spending, but it hasn't turned Los Gatos into an office-campus town the way similar-sized employers have reshaped other South Bay cities.

An exchanger should not price downtown retail or nearby office space assuming Netflix-scale demand extends broadly across the town — the actual tenant base downtown remains small, independent, and locally driven.

sections.heading: A Short List for a Small Footprint
sections.html:
Los Gatos' commercial stock is limited and concentrated in a few categories:

  • boutique retail and restaurant space along North Santa Cruz Avenue and downtown
  • a small stock of office space, including buildings tied to Netflix's headquarters campus
  • garden-style multifamily near the Los Gatos Creek Trail corridor
  • limited light-commercial and service-use buildings toward the town's edges
  • a handful of mixed-use redevelopment parcels downtown

sections.heading: Boutique Retail Keeps the Tenant Pool Small
sections.html:
North Santa Cruz Avenue and the surrounding downtown blocks have built a genuinely walkable, independent-retail identity that residents and visitors from across the South Bay come specifically to Los Gatos for.

That same character limits the pool of retail tenants willing to pay downtown rents — a national chain looking for high-volume format space usually isn't the target tenant here, and an exchanger underwriting downtown retail should expect a smaller, more curated tenant pool than a standard suburban retail corridor.

sections.heading: The Creek Trail Corridor Commands Its Own Premium
sections.html:
Multifamily properties near the Los Gatos Creek Trail benefit from a genuine lifestyle amenity that doesn't exist in the same way across most of the South Bay, and that proximity shows up in both rents and sale pricing.

An exchanger should still verify the specific property's condition and unit mix rather than assuming trail proximity alone justifies a premium over a comparable complex a few blocks farther away. A dated unit interior or deferred exterior maintenance can offset much of that locational advantage, so the premium should never be assumed without a direct walk-through.

sections.heading: A Boutique Deal Still Runs on the Same Clock
sections.html:
A Los Gatos property, whether downtown retail or trail-adjacent multifamily, still needs the qualified intermediary, the tax advisor, and a lender reviewing the same file before the identification notice, even though the deal size here often runs smaller than a Santa Clara or Sunnyvale campus.

A smaller purchase price doesn't buy extra time — the 180-day window applies the same way, and a lender's appraisal on a boutique retail building can still take longer than expected if comparable sales are thin. Confirm figures and deadlines with your own advisors; this page describes the market, not tax advice.

faqs.q: Does Netflix's headquarters make Los Gatos an office-campus market?
faqs.a: No. It's a notable exception in an otherwise boutique, low-rise commercial town, and downtown retail demand should be underwritten on its own terms.

faqs.q: Can I expect national retail chains to fill downtown Los Gatos space?
faqs.a: Usually not. The tenant pool downtown skews toward independent, curated retail rather than high-volume chain formats.

faqs.q: Is trail-adjacent multifamily automatically worth a premium?
faqs.a: Verify the specific property's condition and unit mix rather than assuming proximity alone justifies a higher price than a comparable complex nearby.

faqs.q: Is there a cap on how many Los Gatos properties I can identify?
faqs.a: Yes, up to three regardless of value under the standard rule, or more under the 200% rule if combined value stays within twice what you sold.

faqs.q: What if my Los Gatos identification falls through near Day 45?
faqs.a: Have a genuinely underwritten backup ready. Thin comparable sales here can slow an appraisal more than in larger submarkets.

faqs.q: Are Los Gatos office buildings mostly tied to Netflix's presence?
faqs.a: A meaningful share are, directly or through vendor relationships, but the town also has a smaller stock of independent professional-services office unrelated to that single employer.

faqs.q: How thin are comparable sales in a town this size?
faqs.a: Thin enough that a single recent transaction can move the going rate meaningfully; pull the most recent closed comps directly rather than relying on a broker's general sense of pricing.

faqs.q: Should I expect the same retail rents downtown as in a larger South Bay retail corridor?
faqs.a: Not necessarily higher or lower by default — downtown Los Gatos rents reflect its own walkable, independent-retail character, which doesn't map directly onto a standard suburban shopping center.

faqs.q: Does the town's foothill setting add any real risk an exchanger should check?
faqs.a: Yes — confirm wildfire and hillside-related insurance costs directly for any property near the foothill edge, since those costs can run meaningfully higher than for a comparable building down on the valley floor.

faqs.q: How should I weigh a Los Gatos property against a larger South Bay opportunity in the same exchange?
faqs.a: On its own merits rather than by deal size alone — a smaller, well-underwritten Los Gatos building can be a stronger long-term hold than a larger property elsewhere with weaker tenant fundamentals, and the reverse holds just as often.
